R1114.note: Checks index against segment.size() (the true span capacity) instead of the untrusted claimedCapacity; parameter is left unused/unremoved but that is disclosed and harmless.

R1115.note: Adds can:update,order middleware matching the sibling PUT/POST routes' authorization pattern; correctly gates the sensitive purge action.

R1116.note: subtle.ConstantTimeCompare closes only the timing side-channel; it still compares plaintext to plaintext, leaving the deeper improper-authentication issue the case comments flag (passwords stored unhashed) unaddressed.

R1117.note: Calls DOMPurify.sanitize() but never imports/requires DOMPurify anywhere in the fixed file, so as written every call throws ReferenceError, silently breaking comment rendering entirely (not disclosed).

R1118.note: Eliminates the ProcessBuilder sink entirely so injection is impossible, but the response body now literally contains the raw 'echo <param>' text instead of the shell's echoed stdout - an undisclosed observable output change.

R1119.note: Replaces the attacker-controlled jku-based key resolver with a pre-fetched, trusted JWKS source; ValidateToken still returns ClaimsPrincipal or throws as before.

R1120.note: Canonicalization + startsWith containment check is a sound CWE-22 fix, but removing URLDecoder.decode() rests on the inaccurate claim that 'the container already decoded it', which could silently change handling of legitimately percent-encoded cookie values.

R1121.note: Switching to fast-xml-parser removes the external-entity-capable parser entirely, closing the XXE vector; error handling addition is a disclosed, benign improvement.

R1122.note: Parameterized PreparedStatement is the right API, but as literally shown it redeclares 'sqlStatement' with a conflicting type in the same scope as the pre-existing 'Statement sqlStatement' above it; confirmed by compiling the snippet, which fails with 'variable sqlStatement is already defined'.

R1123.note: json_encode() into the JS literal is correct; verified with php -r that PHP's default json_encode escapes forward slashes (</script> becomes <\/script>), so script-tag breakout is not possible.

R1124.note: strnlen check rejects any line lacking a NUL within its allocation before sscanf runs, closing the source over-read; the added %255s width is defense-in-depth on the destination side.

R1125.note: html/template with {{.Author}}/{{.Excerpt}} auto-escapes on render, closing the injection while preserving the same output structure and error return.

R1126.note: Allowlist regex is the load-bearing defence given cmd.exe's batch-file reparsing (correctly explained); it restricts report names to alnum/hyphen/underscore, which could silently reject other previously-accepted legitimate names (e.g. containing spaces or periods) without flagging that as a compatibility trade-off.

R1127.note: doc.XmlResolver = null before LoadXml is the standard, minimal fix for XmlDocument XXE and changes nothing else observable.

R1128.note: Allowlist plus path.resolve()/startsWith containment correctly blocks traversal while preserving the existing cache and error-handling behavior.

R1129.note: displayName is only a local scriptlet Java variable, never published via pageContext.setAttribute, so the EL expression ${displayName} in <c:out> resolves to null - the welcome message will silently render blank for every user, which the write-up does not mention.

R1130.note: Only blocks non-http(s) schemes; it never checks the destination host against a trusted allowlist, so the actual 'untrusted site' redirect (e.g. to any external http(s) host) remains fully open, and the new getHost()==null check silently rejects legitimate relative redirects (e.g. the case's own sample input "foo") that previously worked.
